Italian Telecom Sector Reports Steady Growth in Q1 Trade Figures

Italy’s telecommunications sector has reported a steady performance in the first quarter of 2024, with industry data showing modest but stable growth across fixed and mobile segments. The Italian Association of Telecommunications Operators (AITO) released its quarterly bulletin on Tuesday, highlighting a 2.1% year-on-year increase in overall revenue for the industry, reaching €8.92 billion in Q1.

Mobile subscriptions continued to outnumber fixed lines, with 85.3 million active SIM cards reported at the end of March, up 0.8% from the previous quarter. Prepaid plans remained the preferred choice for Italian consumers, accounting for 65% of all mobile lines. Fixed broadband connections rose by 1.3% compared to Q1 2023, totaling 19.7 million lines, driven primarily by increased fibre-to-the-home (FTTH) adoption in urban centers.

AITO President Francesca Rinaldi commented on the figures, stating, “The sector’s growth reflects ongoing investment in next-generation networks and the resilience of Italian operators in a competitive marketplace. We are seeing gradual migration from legacy copper to fibre and a steady uptake of 5G services.”

Average revenue per user (ARPU) in the mobile segment remained largely unchanged at €11.40 per month, while fixed broadband ARPU edged up to €24.70, according to the AITO report. Industry analysts say this stability reflects mature market dynamics and ongoing price competition among leading providers such as Teleconnect Italia, NovaTel, and ReteUno.

Wholesale market activity also showed positive trends. The volume of wholesale broadband lines leased to alternative operators rose by 2.5%, reflecting continued demand for infrastructure-based competition. “The healthy growth in wholesale lines is a testament to the robust regulatory environment in Italy, which encourages market entry and network sharing,” said Luca Ferraro, telecoms analyst at Rome-based consultancy Infometrics.

Employment figures in the sector held steady at approximately 92,000, with no major workforce adjustments reported. The AITO bulletin noted ongoing recruitment in network engineering and customer support roles, particularly in regions investing in digital infrastructure upgrades.

Looking ahead, sector representatives remain optimistic. “As digitalisation initiatives continue under Italy’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan, we expect gradual but sustained growth in both urban and rural connectivity,” Rinaldi said. “The industry is well-positioned to meet evolving consumer and business needs.”
